definitions.reading: Points per 100 shots against the average player, adjusted for who else was on the floor. Zero is average. Positive is always good: defence signs are flipped, so +1.5 dTS means opponents shot about 1.5 points worse per 100 shots with this player on the floor.
definitions.shot: A shot is a field-goal attempt or a 2-shot or 3-shot free-throw trip. And-ones, technicals, flagrants, clear-path and other one-shot trips add free-throw value but no shot, because they replaced no possession. Possessions with no attempt carry no weight.
definitions.ts: TS: actual field-goal points, and each shooter's expected free-throw value. TS = SQ + Make + FT.
definitions.sq: SQ: the quality of the looks. CourtLens' expected field-goal points before the shot, plus avg_pts / 2 or avg_pts / 3 per free throw of a 2-shot or 3-shot trip (the value of the possession the foul replaced).
definitions.make: Make (dContest on defence): actual field-goal points minus expected. It holds everything the model cannot see, including how well the shot was contested.
definitions.ft: FT: expected free-throw value above the foul-type baseline. It rewards getting to the line and shooting well there. Actual free-throw results are not used: the expected value comes from the shooter's earlier attempts and R03's league prior.
definitions.interval: 80% game-bootstrap interval (200 replicates) at a fixed penalty and a fixed expected-shot model, so it understates total uncertainty. Overlapping intervals do not rank two players.
definitions.scale: One-season fits at alpha 3000 with no box prior and no time decay, so values are heavily shrunk and are not comparable with Databallr's three-year numbers.

method: Four parallel ridge regressions on the same R01 possessions, the same lineups and the same penalty, each scoring the attempts differently (Databallr's method).

TS = SQ + Make + FT holds on every attempt by construction. One penalty on one design makes ridge linear in the target, so the player coefficients add up as well, and the second-stage regression recovers coefficients of 1 with R² of 1. That check confirms the arithmetic; it says nothing about whether the split is right.

Expected field-goal points come from the accepted R05 model, LightGBM with 31 leaves, calibrated on 2023-24 and never refitted. It has no defender or tracking data. A per-season additive shift makes Make average zero, as Databallr does.
Served for 2022-23 to 2025-26, the seasons the R05 model was not trained on. 2022-23 chose the model and 2023-24 fitted its calibration.
Foul-type baselines per free throw: 2-shot avg_pts / 2, 3-shot avg_pts / 3, and every other trip 0. avg_pts is the season's actual field-goal points per attempt.
Expected FT%: R03's league prior plus the shooter's attempts on earlier dates in this season and the three before it. Nothing at or after the trip is read.
summary.reference_note: Design reference: a saved copy of Databallr's ShotQuality RAPM page. Reproduced: the offence, defence and combined views, the oTS / oSQ / oMake / oFT columns, the minimum and team filters, the CSV, How to Read, the glossary, the four regressions, the foul baselines and the second-stage check. Added: intervals and the persistence check. Different: one-season fits, not three years with time decay; a model without tracking data, not the ShotQuality feed. Not reproduced: Databallr's table values.
summary.credit: The four regressions, foul-type baselines and second-stage check are Databallr's method (databallr.com ShotQuality RAPM page); the expected-value concept is ShotQuality's. CourtLens does not use the paid ShotQuality feed, and its numbers are its own. Data: NBA Stats via shufinskiy/nba_data.

definitions.dsq: D-SQ: points per 100 matchup attempts by which shooters scored less (plus) or more (minus) than their own season shooting against every other defender predicts, relative to the league. Positive is good.
definitions.xpps: Expected PPS: what these shooters' own season 2P% and 3P% predict for the shots they took in this matchup, shrunk toward R03's league prior. It describes who the defender guarded and how many 3s they took. It is not a shot-quality estimate: matchup rows have no shot location. It is neither good nor bad.
definitions.pps: Actual PPS: field-goal points per matchup attempt. Free throws are excluded.
definitions.fga: Matchup FGA: attempts by the player this defender was tracked on. Some 2-pointers are credited to more than one defender, so this overstates distinct shots.
definitions.rapm: D-SQ RAPM: dSQ from the ShotQuality decomposition, the lineup-adjusted effect on the opponents' expected shot value, per 100 shots. Served from 2022-23. A different measurement from the matchup D-SQ: it uses shot location and lineups, not matchups.
definitions.interval: 95% bootstrap over the defender's games (2,000 replicates), with shooters' expected rates held fixed. It shows matchup-outcome noise. Overlapping intervals do not rank two defenders.
definitions.hindsight: Descriptive and in hindsight: a shooter's expected rate uses his whole season, including games after the matchup.

defense_summary.reference_note: Design reference: a saved copy of Databallr's D-ShotQuality page. Reproduced: the ranked player cards, the All / 2PT / 3PT switch, shots defended, an expected and an actual PPS with ranks, the RAPM headline, Key Matchups and next-six paging. Different: expected PPS is what the shooters' own shooting predicts, not ShotQuality's tracking value. Not reproduced: the 2nd Defender column (help columns are zero in every row of the free matchup data), a Closest Defender split (these rows are tracked matchups, not the nearest defender at each shot) and the Data Source switch. Added: the D-SQ value, its interval and the signal and persistence checks. NBA tracking's season closest-defender numbers remain on the Tracking page.
defense_summary.credit: The card layout and the concept are Databallr's D-ShotQuality page; ShotQuality owns the tracking values, which are not used here. Data: NBA Stats matchups via shufinskiy/nba_data.
